citation.title: Numerical Analysis of an FRP-Strengthened Masonry Arch Bridge

document.accessNote: Open-access article (CC BY 4.0); full text retrieved on 2026-08-16. It contains quoted data from Borri et al. 2011 (arch tests) and Page 1987 (Prestwood bridge test); those quoted values are recorded with kind 'quoted' and carry both locations.

abstract: In this paper, the results of an experimental campaign carried out on masonry arches strengthened with one FRP layer applied at the structure intrados are used to calibrate a numerical analysis model. Then, the model is used to predict the contribution that this type of strengthening would have had on the well-known Prestwood Bridge. The numerical results show that the hypothetical intervention of the Prestwood Bridge would imply an increase in the ultimate load of the structure, although it would be significantly lower than that usually obtained for the case of arches tested in laboratory.

specimens.label: Borri et al. 2011 unstrengthened arch (as reported by Simoncello et al. 2020)
specimens.tierRationale: Direct geometry and load (mid-span concentrated load on a 2 m span arch), but the data are quoted from a secondary open source (Simoncello et al. 2020) because the primary paper (Borri et al. 2011, Composites Part B) is closed access. Values are marked 'quoted' and should be re-verified against the primary full text before use as acceptance criteria.

specimens.label: Prestwood bridge destructive test (Page 1987), as modeled by Simoncello et al. 2020
specimens.tierRationale: Full-scale bridge with fill. Our model can represent the arch ring, the fill as load, and the patch load, but not the passive backfill interaction or the deformable abutments, which are known contributions.

span.location: Simoncello et al. 2020, Masonry Arch Bridge section and Figure 7B (span L)

tensileStrength.notes: Table 4 lists an additional masonry column value (0.001); column header mapping is ambiguous in the retrieved text and is therefore not transcribed.

loading.description: In-situ test (Page 1987): distributed load over a 300 mm long section along the span over the entire arch width at one quarter of the span; modeled through a 300 x 3800 mm rigid zone.

loadPatchLength.location: Simoncello et al. 2020, Masonry Arch Bridge section

peakLoad.location: Simoncello et al. 2020, Unstrengthened Bridge section (maximum applied load measured on site, quoting Page 1987)

numericalPeakLoad.location: Simoncello et al. 2020, Unstrengthened Bridge section (numerical analysis, good agreement with the experimental one)

numericalDisplacementAtPeak.location: Simoncello et al. 2020, Strengthened Bridge section (unstrengthened model)

observables.failureMode: Collapse mechanism with plastic hinge locations in good agreement with the experimental cracking (Figures 7A, 8B-D); fill provides strength in addition to its weight.

curves.figure: Simoncello et al. 2020, Figure 9 (numerical curve with experimental maximum marker)
curves.content: Load vs arch control-point displacement, unstrengthened

specimens.label: Prestwood bridge with hypothetical full-intrados FRP strengthening (numerical)
specimens.tierRationale: Pure numerical prediction with no experimental strengthened counterpart; useful for mechanism and effectiveness comparison, not for direct load validation.

loading.description: Same patch load as the unstrengthened case.

reinforcement.type: One FRP layer applied to the entire intrados surface with spike anchors
reinforcement.bondModel: Bilinear bond-slip law, tau-f = 1.1 MPa, su = 0.4 mm (Table 5).

strengthIncreaseVsExperimental.location: Simoncello et al. 2020, Strengthened Bridge section (increase in peak load with respect to the unstrengthened experimental peak)

strengthIncreaseVsNumerical.location: Simoncello et al. 2020, Strengthened Bridge section (with respect to the unstrengthened numerical peak)

derivedStrengthenedPeak.location: Derived as 228 kN x 1.43 from the quoted experimental peak and the stated 43% increase
derivedStrengthenedPeak.notes: Only approximate: the 43% applies to the numerical peak-load definition.

displacementAtPeakStrengthened.location: Simoncello et al. 2020, Strengthened Bridge section

observables.failureMode: Peak defined by masonry crushing; FRP not fully exploited (about 60% of the debonding capacity tau-f=1.1 MPa).

extractionNotes: Full text retrieved from the Frontiers open-access page on 2026-08-16.

Values that originate from Borri et al. 2011 or Page 1987 are marked 'quoted' and record the quoting location in this paper; they must be re-verified against the primary sources before being used as acceptance criteria.
Tables 1-5 are partially image-based; column headers are reconstructed from the surrounding text. Where the column mapping is ambiguous the value is not transcribed and is noted as UNKNOWN.
The published Table 3 lists the FRP modulus as '20,5000'; the same material appears as 205,000 MPa in Table 4. Both are recorded as stated.
Load-displacement figures (Figures 5, 6, 9) are digitizable; not digitized in this step.
